content.overview: BNS s. 104 — Punishment for murder by life-convict.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Punishment for murder by life-convict. BNS restatement of IPC 303. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 303. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 104 is the rule on “Punishment for murder by life-convict”. The section provides that whoever, being under sentence of imprisonment for life, commits murder, shall be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, which shall mean the remainder of that person’s natural life. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 104 exists so that “Punishment for murder by life-convict” has a closed legal test in Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Homicide, organised crime, terrorism, hurt, acid, restraint, assault, kidnapping and trafficking.

The provision in detail
104. Whoever, being under sentence of imprisonment for life, commits murder, shall be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, which shall mean the remainder of that person’s natural life

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever, being under sentence of imprisonment for life, commits murder, shall be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, which shall mean the remainder of that person’s natural life

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 104 (Punishment for murder by life-convict) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 104 (Punishment for murder by life-convict), Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever, being under sentence of imprisonment for life, commits murder, shall be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, which shall mean the remainder of that person’s natural life
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 104 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 104 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.
